stem:
Meera's teacher places a few grains of potassium permanganate into a beaker of water. The colour slowly spreads through the water without any stirring.

Which statement correctly explains why the colour spreads and how using hotter water would change this?

options.text: The colour spreads because water particles are in constant motion, and the colour spreads faster in hotter water because the particles move faster.
The colour spreads only because the beaker is shaken, and the temperature of the water makes no difference.
The colour spreads because water particles are still, and the colour spreads more slowly in hotter water.
The colour spreads because the grains push the water aside, and hotter water stops the colour from spreading.

teacher.key_rationale: Colour spreads through water by diffusion, driven by the constant motion of water particles; at higher temperature particles move faster, so spreading is faster in hotter water. Only option A states both ideas correctly. B wrongly requires shaking and denies the temperature effect; C claims particles are still and reverses the temperature effect; D gives a false mechanism and reverses the temperature effect.
